newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps firmer, fuel steady at lower levels.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps firmer, fuel steady at lower levels.

text.p: European oil swaps were steady to firmer in late trade on Tuesday, supported by firmer crude. After sustaining early losses fuel oil swaps steadied amid active trade at the lower level, traders said.

Crude and gas oil firmed on tighter supply and good demand, high sulphur fuel swaps were steady at the lower levels after seeing early pressure from weaker low sulphur trade while gasoline and naphtha were steady to firmer with crude.
Brent crude contracts for difference (CFDs) were firmer with some good buying seen from one trade house.
Prompt differentials had slipped in early business while distant weeks steadied slightly with physical avails tighter.

This week's CFDs were offered three cents weaker at June Brent -34 cents in the morning but edged up to trade around -32 cents later. The current week/next week roll traded flat and next week traded up to June -30 after dipping to -35 cents.
Further out May 12-16 was four cents firmer at around June Brent -31/-26 cents while May 19-23 CFDs talked five cents firmer at June Brent -29/-25 cents.
Longer term crude swaps were steady, though showing only a narrow contango spanning 30 cents to the end of the year.

Gasoline swap quotes were notional as good physical supply kept buying interest thin. However, traders expected the market to pick up a little soon. This sentiment was reflected in a $2-3 backwardation for May contracts over June.
"We're pretty bullish for May and June...We've seen very little since the buying spree in April," one trader said.
May swaps valued steady around $195.50 with June at $193 a tonne fob ARA.
Naphtha talk was thin but prices edged higher with crude.
May swaps firmed $1.50 to $181/$182 a tonne with June at $183.00/$184.00 and July valued near $184, also up $1.50.
Gas oil swaps continued firm up as volatility to the upside with May gas oil futures breaking $167 resistance in early trade fuelling good buying for swaps.
"The good physical buying and lack of sellers is causing people to load up with swaps as a hedge against the volatility," a broker said.
EN590 May contracts were bid at $13.50, up from $12 last Friday while May 0.2 sulphur swaps were bid at $5, $1 firmer and June talked $3.50/$4 as premiums to the IPE.

EN590/0.2 sulphur differentials were actively traded with May done at a slightly firmer $8.75, June at $8.25 and $8.75 after finishing last Friday at around $7.50/$8. Further out Q3 contracts differentials traded at $8 a couple of time and $8.25.

Heavy fuel swaps eased on renewed pressure from low sulphur which was offered 50 cents to $1 a tonne below late Monday levels in early business but good buying interest at the lower levels steadied prices later.
May barge swaps traded actively between $81.25 and $82 while June traded at $82 and $82.50 and July at $85.50 fob ARA.
The third quarter was heading toward $85 in early business having traded at $85.50 and $85.75 on Monday, but strengthened later to trade at $86 and $85.75.
May low sulphur swaps traded $84.25 up to $85 cif NWE, steadying after meeting strong selling pressure in early business following weaker spot market trade at $95 cif Italy.
June contracts were traded at $87 and $86.75 fob NWE
--London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7456
